paragraphs: The Freelander SD4 was introduced in 2011 as a higher-output diesel variant within the L359 generation, sitting above the eD4 and TD4. It uses the Ford Duratorq 2.2-litre four-cylinder diesel — a widely used unit across Ford and Land Rover models of that era. The SD4's higher output shares the same underlying Duratorq pattern as the lower-powered eD4, with the same known wear points: injector failure and DPF clogging are the most consistently reported issues. The Freelander is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road. cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the Freelander SD4 from 2023 to present. The engine features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older engine V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every engine rebuild.
